quests.instruction: The word “light” has more than one meaning. In which sentence does “light” mean the opposite of “heavy”?
quests.correctAnswer: The kitten was light enough to carry in one hand.
options: The kitten was light enough to carry in one hand.
The room was light after the curtains opened.
quests.hint: Which sentence is about how much something weighs?
quests.explanation: “Light” can mean not heavy, full of brightness, or a lamp. Only the first sentence is about weight.
quests.funFact: A newborn kitten weighs only about a hundred grams.

quests.instruction: In which sentence does “hard” mean the opposite of “easy”?
quests.correctAnswer: The maths test was hard, so many students needed extra time.
options: The ice was hard and cold under their boots.
Hard bread can be softened in milk.
The maths test was hard, so many students needed extra time.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence about effort, not about touch.
quests.explanation: “Hard” can mean difficult or firm. The opposite of difficult is easy, while the opposite of firm is soft.
quests.funFact: Scientists use the Mohs scale to rate how hard different minerals are.

quests.instruction: In which sentence does “short” mean the opposite of “tall”?
quests.correctAnswer: The short boy stood beside his tall brother.
options: The short boy stood beside his tall brother.
The pencil got short after sharpening.
We took a short break between classes.
quests.hint: Which sentence compares two people’s heights?
quests.explanation: “Short” can describe height, length or time. Only the first sentence is the opposite of “tall”.
quests.funFact: The word “short” also hides inside “shortcut” and “shorts”.

quests.instruction: In which sentence does “right” mean the opposite of “wrong”?
quests.correctAnswer: Your answer to question five is right.
options: Your answer to question five is right.
quests.hint: Which sentence would a teacher say while marking your work?
quests.explanation: “Right” can mean correct, or the direction opposite of left. Here, only correct answers match “wrong”.
quests.funFact: “Right” can mean correct, a direction or a freedom, like the right to learn.

quests.instruction: In which sentence is “old” the opposite of “young”?
quests.correctAnswer: The old man told stories about his village.
options: That old trick doesn’t work anymore.
My old bag has a broken zip.
The old man told stories about his village.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence about a person’s age.
quests.explanation: For people and animals, the opposite of old is young. For things, the opposite is usually new.
quests.funFact: In some languages, there are different words for “old” when talking about people and things.

quests.instruction: In which sentence does “close” mean the opposite of “far”?
quests.correctAnswer: The bus stop is close to my house.
options: The shop will close at nine.
The bus stop is close to my house.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence about distance.
quests.explanation: “Close” can mean near or shut. Only the first sentence is the opposite of “far”.
quests.funFact: “Close” is pronounced differently when it means near and when it means shut.

quests.instruction: In which sentence is “fair” the opposite of “unfair”?
quests.correctAnswer: It’s only fair that everyone gets a turn.
options: She has fair hair and blue eyes.
We went to the village fair.
It’s only fair that everyone gets a turn.
quests.hint: Which sentence is about being treated equally?
quests.explanation: “Fair” can mean just, light-colored or a fun event with stalls. Only the first meaning has “unfair” as its opposite.
quests.funFact: A fair, with rides and stalls, is a very old kind of gathering.

quests.instruction: The railway station at 8 a.m. is bustling. At 3 a.m., with no trains and no passengers, it is…
quests.hint: Picture a platform at 3 a.m.
quests.explanation: Bustling means busy and full of people. Deserted means empty, with nobody around.
quests.funFact: Some big railway stations handle hundreds of thousands of passengers every day.

quests.instruction: A magnet pulls an iron nail toward it: it attracts the nail. When two magnets meet the wrong way round, they push apart. They…
quests.hint: Try pressing two matching magnet ends together.
quests.explanation: To attract is to pull toward. To repel is to push away.
quests.funFact: The word “magnet” comes from Magnesia, a region of ancient Greece where magnetic stones were found.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT mean the opposite of “slow”?
quests.hint: Which word describes something moving slowly?
quests.explanation: Quick and rapid mean fast, which is the opposite of slow. Sluggish means slow-moving too, so it matches “slow”.
quests.funFact: “Sluggish” comes from “slug”, the slow-moving creature.

quests.instruction: A reliable friend turns up when she says she will. A friend who keeps cancelling at the last minute is…
quests.hint: Think about a friend who keeps cancelling.
quests.explanation: Reliable means you can depend on it. Unreliable means you can’t.
quests.funFact: Smoke alarms have to be reliable, so people test them regularly.

quests.instruction: Most garden ladybirds are harmless to people. Fumes from burning plastic, which can damage your lungs, are…
quests.hint: Fumes from burning plastic aren’t something to breathe in.
quests.explanation: Harmless means it won’t hurt you. Harmful means it can cause damage.
quests.funFact: Ladybirds help gardens because they eat tiny insects called aphids.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the opposite idea: “Although the instructions looked complicated, the game turned out to be surprisingly…”
quests.hint: What did the game turn out to be instead of tricky?
quests.explanation: “Although” signals a surprise. A complicated-looking game that’s easy to play is simple.
quests.funFact: Many classic games, such as noughts and crosses, have very simple rules.

quests.instruction: In the sentence “The bus came early, but the train was late,” which two words are opposites?
quests.hint: Look for two words about arriving at opposite times.
quests.explanation: “Early” and “late” sit on opposite sides of the expected time. The other pairs are just different kinds of words.
quests.funFact: Some trains run on such tight schedules that a delay of a minute is counted as late.

quests.instruction: Complete the saying: “Easy come, easy…”
quests.hint: Think of the reverse of “come”.
quests.explanation: The saying uses opposites to make a point: things that arrive effortlessly often leave the same way.
quests.funFact: This saying has been used in English for hundreds of years.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that describes the opposite of “The shop was crowded and noisy”.
quests.correctAnswer: The shop was empty and silent.
options: The shop was empty and noisy.
The shop was empty and silent.
The shop was crowded and silent.
quests.hint: Both ideas need to flip.
quests.explanation: Crowded flips to empty and noisy flips to silent. Choices that flip only one idea aren’t true opposites.
quests.funFact: Many shops are busiest on weekends.

quests.instruction: Which of these pairs contains two words that are opposites?
quests.hint: Look for the pair that sits at opposite ends.
quests.explanation: Ancient things are from long ago, and modern things are from now. Tidy and clean are related, and tiny and small mean nearly the same.
quests.funFact: A thesaurus lists synonyms, while an antonym dictionary lists opposites.

quests.instruction: Which pair of words do NOT have opposite meanings?
quests.hint: Look for the pair in which both words mean the same.
quests.explanation: Begin and start mean the same thing. The other two pairs pull in opposite directions.
quests.funFact: English has many words with the same meaning because it borrowed words from other languages.

quests.instruction: In the relay, Team A is ahead by three metres. That means Team B is…
quests.hint: Where is Team B compared with Team A?
quests.explanation: Ahead means in front, and behind means at the back.
quests.funFact: In a close race, the lead can change many times.

quests.instruction: In the quiz game, Isha’s team gained 10 points for a correct answer. For each wrong answer, it ___ 5 points.
quests.hint: Points can be won and points can slip away.
quests.explanation: To gain is to get something. To lose is to have less of it.
quests.funFact: Many board games use points to keep track of who is winning.

quests.instruction: The cook said, “Sorry, the soup is too salty.” Which word describes the opposite problem, soup with hardly any flavor?
quests.hint: Think about a problem you would fix by adding salt.
quests.explanation: Too salty has too much flavor. Bland has too little.
quests.funFact: Salt has been used to preserve and flavor food for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: In which sentence is “cool” the opposite of “warm”?
quests.correctAnswer: The lake water felt cool after the hot walk.
options: The lake water felt cool after the hot walk.
He stayed cool during the emergency.
quests.hint: Which sentence is about temperature?
quests.explanation: “Cool” can mean a little cold, fashionable or calm. Only the first sentence is about temperature.
quests.funFact: People have used the word “cool” to mean “great” for about a hundred years.

quests.instruction: In which sentence does “dry” mean the opposite of “wet”?
options: The speech was dry and boring.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that talks about water.
quests.explanation: “Dry” can mean without water, dull, or flat in tone. Only the first one is the opposite of wet.
quests.funFact: The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth.

quests.instruction: In which sentence is “plain” the opposite of “fancy”?
quests.correctAnswer: She wore a plain white dress to the wedding.
options: She wore a plain white dress to the wedding.
He explained it in plain English.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence about decoration.
quests.explanation: “Plain” can mean undecorated, clear or a flat area of land. Only the first is the opposite of fancy.
quests.funFact: “Plain” also names large flat areas of land, such as the Great Plains.

quests.instruction: Which sentence has a pair of opposites in it?
quests.correctAnswer: The lights went out suddenly, but the sun rose gradually.
options: The sun rose suddenly and quickly.
The lights went out suddenly, but the sun rose gradually.
The lights went out and the sun rose.
quests.hint: Which sentence uses two opposite ways of happening?
quests.explanation: Sudden means all at once, and gradual means little by little. Only one sentence uses both.
quests.funFact: Dawn can take more than an hour from first light to full sunrise.

quests.instruction: Instead of forgiving her friend for the mistake, Tia chose to ___ her.
quests.hint: Think about letting go of something versus holding on.
quests.explanation: Forgiving lets an error go; blaming holds the person responsible.
quests.funFact: Many cultures have sayings about forgiving and moving on.

quests.instruction: Buses on Route 5 come every five minutes: frequent. Buses on Route 9 come only twice a day, which is…
quests.hint: One route has a bus every five minutes.
quests.explanation: Frequent means happening often. Rare means happening only seldom.
quests.funFact: Cities use “frequency” to describe how often a bus or train arrives.

quests.instruction: Read the notice: “The pool is OPEN to members only. It is CLOSED on Mondays for cleaning.” Which two words are opposites?
quests.hint: Which pair describes whether you can go in?
quests.explanation: Open means people can use it. Closed means they can’t. The other pairs aren’t opposites.
quests.funFact: Swimming pools have to be cleaned regularly, which is why many close one day each week.

quests.instruction: Mangoes got the most votes in the class poll. Which sentence gives the opposite result?
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that puts mangoes at the bottom.
quests.explanation: Most means the biggest number; least or fewest means the smallest number.
quests.funFact: India is one of the largest producers of mangoes in the world.

quests.instruction: On a day at the seaside, which pair of words describes opposite kinds of weather or water?
quests.hint: Look for one peaceful word and one wild word.
quests.explanation: Calm means still and peaceful. Stormy means wild and rough. Quiet and windy don’t reverse each other.
quests.funFact: Sailors use a scale numbered 0 to 12, called the Beaufort scale, to describe wind.
